author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit can be corrected: the form opens prefilled with the visit's current date and description, booking-time validation applies, and a successful correction updates that visit in place before the owner's record is shown.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction form for a booked visit shows that visit's current date and description prefilled
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit in place, adds no additional visit to the pet, and shows the owner's record
Submitting a blank description refuses the correction and names the description
Submitting a date of today or earlier refuses the correction and names the date
non_goals: A visible entry point to the correction form on the owner detail page
notes: Reuse the pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm template and its visit model attribute. GET and POST share /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; POST redirects to the owner detail page on success and redisplays the form on validation failure. The form is reachable by URL only in this slice — no owner-detail link (recorded as an open question). NG-5 was narrowed 2026-08-23; see adr/2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: REQ-VIS-003 is the create-or-update controller pattern the codebase already demonstrates in PetController, applied to Visit. No new module, type, or pattern. It fits the observed shape in system-design.md (State Machine: pet workflows branch on isNew to choose insert vs update; VisitController is the visit-booking controller writing through OwnerRepository). PetController.findPet (branch on an optional petId path variable: new Pet() vs owner.getPet(petId)) and updatePetDetails (mutate the existing persisted instance's fields, then saveAndFlush(owner)) are the exact template for the GET-prefill and POST-in-place-update the correction needs. Booking validation is reused verbatim from VisitController.processNewVisitForm (blank-description via @NotBlank, non-future date rejected with typeMismatch.visitDate). Oracle N/A: IntelliJ MCP tools are not in this dispatch's toolset; patterns cited via Read of PetController/Owner/Visit/Pet.
integration_points: GET and POST share /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit; POST redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} on success and redisplays pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm on validation failure — same redirect/redisplay shape as processNewVisitForm.
No repository change: Visit is written through OwnerRepository.save(owner) via cascade, the sole write path for the owner-pet-visit graph.

The template already branches on visit['new'] for the heading and the previous-visits table; the correction (visit['new'] == false, i.e. a persisted visit) reuses the same form/model attribute unchanged.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute findPet branches on @PathVariable(name=..., required=false) Integer id: null -> new instance, else load existing from the aggregate. The visit model attribute must adopt this branch keyed on visitId.

updatePetDetails: fetch the existing instance by id, mutate its fields in place (setters), saveAndFlush(owner). This is the in-place-update mechanism — same instance, same persisted id, cascade issues UPDATE not INSERT. Mirror it for date/description on the existing Visit.

Owner.getPet(Integer id) is the existing by-id lookup within the aggregate. Pet has no equivalent getVisit(Integer id); the implementer supplies the visit lookup either as a symmetric Pet.getVisit(Integer id) accessor (preferred for consistency) or inline over pet.getVisits().

risks.risk: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit (@ModelAttribute("visit")) unconditionally does new Visit() + pet.addVisit(visit). @ModelAttribute methods run before EVERY handler in the controller, so if the edit routes are added without changing it, every GET/POST to the edit route creates a phantom new visit AND fails to prefill the existing one — directly violating both 'shows current date/description' and 'adds no additional visit'.
risks.mitigation: Make the visit model attribute branch on an optional visitId path variable (mirror PetController.findPet): visitId present -> return the existing Visit fetched by id from the pet's collection; absent (the /visits/new route) -> keep new Visit() + addVisit as today.

risks.risk: The InitBinder disallows id and *.id, so the visit's persisted id cannot arrive via the form. If the POST binds onto a fresh Visit (transient, id == null), cascade INSERTs a second row instead of updating in place.
risks.mitigation: The correction must mutate the SAME persisted Visit instance loaded server-side by visitId (which carries its id) and set date/description on it, then owners.save(owner). Do not construct a new Visit on the edit path.

risks.risk: Pet.addVisit(Visit) has no isNew guard (unlike Owner.addPet, which guards on pet.isNew()). Calling addVisit with an already-persisted visit would attempt to add a second element to the visits set, risking a duplicate-identity cascade.
risks.mitigation: On the edit path never call addVisit; only mutate the existing element's fields. Reserve addVisit for the booking (new) path.

notes: Durable-memory write this dispatch: added the ADR index row for 2026-08-23-non-goal-visit-correction-narrowing.md to docs/adr/README.md (owned by system-design-expert; the non-goal ADR was authored by product-requirements-expert, which cannot write the index). This is ADR bookkeeping, not an architecture change — the verdict stays covered. author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Ownership chain is enforced end-to-end in loadPetWithVisit: owner is resolved by ownerId, pet must belong to that owner (owner.getPet(petId) throws when absent), and the visit must belong to that pet (pet.getVisit(visitId) searches only that pets visit set and returns null otherwise). A visitId from another pet/owner cannot be updated, so the edit path introduces no IDOR beyond the sample apps existing no-auth design.

InitBinder disallows id and *.id, so neither the visits identifier nor any nested id can be rebound. Combined with the absence of a visit->pet association field on the Visit side (the pet_id join column is owned by Pet.visits), a caller cannot reassign a visit to a different pet or owner via mass assignment.

In-place update is data-integrity sound: processUpdateVisitForm binds the persisted Visit instance loaded via visitId (same object graph as owner->pet->visits), so owners.save(owner) cascades an UPDATE rather than inserting a duplicate visit. No new visit is added.
No new injection surface: description remains user text rendered through Thymeleaf auto-escaping (pre-existing), and no SQL/command/deserialization sink is introduced.
The Owner mass-assignment surface (binding @ModelAttribute Owner then saving) is the pre-existing processNewVisitForm pattern, not newly introduced by this change; *.id rebinding is blocked.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: When visitId is non-null, loadPetWithVisit returns pet.getVisit(visitId) without a null check. Pet.getVisit(Integer) documents it returns null when no matching visit exists for the pet. A stale or invalid visitId in the URL (e.g. /owners/1/pets/1/visits/999/edit) silently produces null as the visit model attribute, causing a NullPointerException in processUpdateVisitForm at visit.getDate() before any application logic runs. The pet lookup directly above (lines 71-74) correctly throws IllegalArgumentException when the pet is null — that same guard is missing for the visit. Fix: extract the return value and throw when null: Visit visit = pet.getVisit(visitId); if (visit == null) { throw new IllegalArgumentException("Visit with id " + visitId + " not found for pet with id " + petId + "."); } return visit;

org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.support.RedirectAttributes (a Spring import) is grouped with jakarta.validation.Valid without a blank line separator. PetController — the template this slice explicitly mirrors — separates each import group with its own blank line (PetController.java lines 35-39). The formatter accepts both arrangements, but the inconsistency makes RedirectAttributes read as part of the jakarta group rather than the Spring group.
findings.fix: Add a blank line between line 31 (import jakarta.validation.Valid;) and line 32 (import org.springframework.web.servlet.mvc.support.RedirectAttributes;) to match PetController import grouping.

approved_aspects: loadPetWithVisit correctly branches on visitId: null path preserves the existing booking flow (new Visit + addVisit); non-null path fetches the persisted instance, satisfying the design-block risk mitigations for phantom-visit creation and in-place-update semantics.

processUpdateVisitForm mutates the persisted Visit in place via data binding and saves through owners.save(owner), ensuring cascade issues UPDATE not INSERT — correct mirror of the updatePetDetails pattern.

Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer id) in structure (isNew guard before id comparison, Objects.equals for null-safe equality, null return for not-found) and carries the same Javadoc style — consistent-with-codebase.

Validation logic in processUpdateVisitForm (blank description via @NotBlank, non-future date via rejectValue) is byte-for-byte identical to processNewVisitForm — no duplication of rules, no inconsistency.
initUpdateVisitForm / processUpdateVisitForm naming follows the initNewVisitForm / processNewVisitForm convention exactly.

Format check passed (checkFormatMain BUILD SUCCESSFUL). IDE not consulted — oracle tools not in dispatch toolset; consistent-with-codebase claim for Pet.getVisit backed by direct Read of Owner.getPet(Integer id) at Owner.java:117-127 confirming the null-return aggregate-lookup pattern.

author: change-grader
summary: add visit-correction edit flow mirroring booking

blast_radius.note: Contained in the owner package: Pet.java gains a getVisit lookup, VisitController.java adds the edit GET/POST pair and an optional visitId to loadPetWithVisit, plus matching tests and PRD/ADR docs. 55 prod lines, 2 modules, no sensitive paths.

semantic_surprise.note: The correction path faithfully mirrors booking: same future-date rule (!isAfter(now)), reuses loadPetWithVisit which returns the persisted visit so binding mutates it in place and owners.save cascades an UPDATE not an INSERT. getVisit guards new/unsaved visits and null-checks the miss. No hidden behavior change.

test_adequacy.note: Six new tests assert real outcomes at the boundaries: prefill of current date/description, not-found rejection, in-place update proving the visit count stays 1 with new values, redirect target, blank-description refusal, and non-future-date refusal with the exact error code.

reviewer_hedging.note: Round-1 blocked finding (missing null check on getVisit) and the autofixes were resolved; round-2 shows all four reviewers approved with empty findings. No escalate or bar_clause hedges.

scope_deviation.note: design_revisions=0, consultations=0, build_retries=0. The diff matches REQ-VIS-003 exactly; docs narrow NG-5 with a supporting ADR, and the URL-only reachability (no visible link) is a deliberately documented, deferred boundary, not creep.

rationale: A tightly-scoped edit flow that mirrors the existing booking controller with the same validation and in-place-update semantics, backed by real boundary tests and clean unanimous re-approval. Confirm and merge; a fast read of VisitController's edit POST and getVisit is enough.
